issues.description: The problem statement requires implementing get_status to return a simple boolean (1 byte) in AL ("Implementieren Sie `get_status`, welche einen simplen Boolean (1 Byte) in `al` zurückgibt"). The template provides a get_status implementation that moves the address of the hello string into EAX (32-bit) — i.e. `mov eax, hello` — which does not match the required 1-byte boolean-in-AL behavior and will confuse students about the expected return convention.
issues.suggested_fix: Replace the incorrect implementation in the template with a clear stub that matches the specification (return a boolean in AL). For example, make get_status a one-byte-return stub such as `xor al, al` / `mov al, 1` (depending on intended truth value) followed by `ret`, or leave a TODO stub with the correct register comment. Add a comment clarifying that AL should contain the boolean result. This prevents students from being misled by the current `mov eax, hello` implementation.

issues.description: The solution repository's reference implementation does not include a get_status implementation at all (solution file only contains main and fixes the ecc→ecx issue). Because the problem explicitly asks students to implement get_status and to return a boolean in AL, the absence of get_status in the solution means the solution does not demonstrate the required behavior, creating a cross-artifact inconsistency and denying students a correct reference.
issues.suggested_fix: Add a correct get_status implementation to the solution repository that returns the boolean in AL as specified (e.g., `mov al, 1` / `xor al, al` then `ret`), or explicitly document in the solution that get_status is intentionally omitted (with a note explaining expected AL semantics). Preferably include a short comment showing the intended calling convention and returned value so students have an accurate reference.
